Recommendations: The patient is advised to maintain a diet rich in iron, as well as avoid stressful situations that may trigger a hemolytic crisis.

Reason for consultation: The patient, a 40-year-old woman, comes to the consultation due to fusion of the distal phalanx of the fifth toe, mucopolysaccharide storage syndrome, and chorioretinal coloboma. The fusion of the distal phalanx of the fifth toe presents as an abnormal union of the bones that make up said phalanx, which can hinder mobility and cause discomfort when walking. Mucopolysaccharide storage syndrome is a hereditary metabolic disease that causes the abnormal accumulation of certain types of complex sugars in different tissues and organs of the body, which can cause various health problems. On the other hand, chorioretinal coloboma manifests as a congenital malformation in the structure of the eye, specifically in the choroid and retina, and can affect the patient's visual acuity.

Examinations performed: Imaging tests such as X-rays of the affected foot have been performed, as well as biochemical studies to evaluate the levels of mucopolysaccharides in blood and urine. In addition, a detailed ophthalmological examination has been carried out to assess the chorioretinal coloboma.

Diagnosis: After evaluating the symptoms and the results of the examinations performed, the diagnosis of Hurler Syndrome is established, a form of mucopolysaccharidosis type I, which is characterized by the deficiency of an enzyme that breaks down mucopolysaccharides, leading to their accumulation in different tissues. This syndrome can manifest with fusion of phalanges, ocular alterations such as chorioretinal coloboma, as well as other systemic symptoms.

Treatment: Treatment for Hurler Syndrome includes enzyme replacement therapies, surgical interventions to correct bone deformities, as well as ophthalmological follow-up to monitor possible visual complications.

Recommendations: The patient is advised to maintain regular medical follow-up, follow the treatment prescribed by the medical team and attend follow-up consultations with the corresponding specialists.
